title: The documented GitHub Pages deployment cannot work — no Vite base and no router basename
detail: A project page is served from /<repo>/, which needs vite.config.ts `base` for assets AND react-router `basename` for routes. Neither is set. Assets 404 and every route below / resolves against the wrong path, so the 'live demo' the README leads with would be a blank page. This is the one finding that blocks the actual goal of the project — publishing it — and it pairs with S129: there is no deploy workflow to run either.

title: Resetting the library fires one full library reload per book, concurrently
detail: Promise.all(books.map(removeBook)) and every removeBook ends in reload(), which re-runs listByProfile over the whole store. Deleting 300 books issues 300 concurrent reads of a shrinking library plus 1,200 cascade transactions. Promise.all also means one rejection leaves the library half-deleted with no record of where it stopped.

title: Reset hardcodes a cache key that is exported as a constant and used that way elsewhere
detail: LibraryPage builds the recommendations key from RECS_CACHE_KEY; ProfilePage writes the literal 'booksum.recs.'. Changing the constant silently stops reset from clearing the cache, leaving stale recommendations attached to a library that no longer exists. The daily-wisdom key is a bare literal in both places it appears.

title: Every library mutation hands BookDetail a brand-new Summary object, which is what makes the quiz and chat re-fire
detail: listByProfile returns freshly deserialised objects, so `book` changes identity on every reload; the effect re-runs and setSummary stores another new Summary. QuizModal and ChatModal both depend on that object identity (S057, S116), so an unrelated library change re-generates a paid quiz and silently resets a chat session. This is the upstream cause of both — fixing it here fixes both consumers.

title: The crash screen prints the raw error message to the user
detail: `{message}` is whatever Error.message holds — SDK internals, IndexedDB detail, or a bundler path. It is shown verbatim with no framing, and there is no copy-to-clipboard so a user who wants to report it has to transcribe it by hand.

title: No catch-all route, so an unknown URL renders 'Something went wrong'
detail: A mistyped or stale link falls through to the error element and is presented as a crash rather than as a missing page.

title: onOpenReader declares a Book parameter its implementation ignores
detail: BookDetail's prop type is (book: Book) => void; the page passes () => void navigate(...) and closes over `book` instead. Harmless today, misleading to the next caller.

title: A failed summary lookup is indistinguishable from having no summary
detail: getSummary(...).then(setSummary) has no catch, so a repo error leaves summary undefined and the page renders its 'not summarised yet' state — telling the user the book has no summary when the read simply failed.

title: Crash screen icon chip is light-only
detail: bg-red-50 with no dark variant on a dark:bg-night page.
